## Natural history notes

A small darkling beetle characterized by an elongated oval body, dark brown to black coloration, and a somewhat slender, smooth-sided form typical of Statira beetles. In Florida, Statira basalis is most likely found in warm wooded or semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and areas with leaf litter, bark, dead branches, or decaying wood. Adults and larvae are likely associated with fungi, dead wood, leaf litter, or other organic debris, helping recycle nutrients while serving as prey for spiders, birds, lizards, and other insect-eating animals.
